profile.name: Galbrena
profile.review:
Galbrena is a 5-star Fusion Pistol DPS who, despite what her weapon class would make you think, gets up close and personal with her targets to deal Fusion & Heavy/Echo Skill damage to them under her enhanced state called Demon Hypostasis. Accessing this state and optimizing its damage via Galbrena’s numerous self-buffs included in her kit is the key to unleashing her full potential.

Key Mechanics

Galbrena’s kit focuses around entering a stance called Demon Hypostasis. It allows her to cast massively enhanced attacks that deal the overwhelming majority of her damage at the cost of Forte points called Sinflame. They get converted 1 to 1 into Purging Flame which is then expended to cast her enhanced moves in Demon Hypostasis. As a result, the focus of her kit is generating her max of 100 Sinflame to then expend it after entering Demon Hypostasis, entered by casting her Enhanced Skill.

The amount of Sinflame currently generated is visible on her Forte bar, marked in blue outside of Demon Hypostasis. In Demon Hypostasis, only Purging Flame will be visible.

Via her Inherent Skills, Galbrena possesses Stamina recovery on a lot of her attacks, and a ramp-up DMG Amplify effect up to 20% which is easy to fully stack, as well as 20% ATK which will be up throughout most of her rotation. A lot of self-buffs make for a strong, self-sufficient kit.

Furthermore, she additionally possesses an extra Forte bar marked in red, and it stacks up to 40 points. It is called Afterflame, and it replenishes by casting Echo skills, at a rate of 8 points per. This increases the DMG Taken of enemies during Demon Hypostasis by up to 60% (1.5% per point).

The above is especially important because DMG Taken (also known as Vulnerability) is a multiplier very rarely seen in character kits (mostly high Sequences like Cartethyia’s and Phrolova’s, and Qiuyuan’s Forte buffs). In most cases, it is rare enough to be considered a completely unique multiplier that buffs overall damage by whatever percentage is indicated. In other words, Galbrena’s damage increases by up to 60% with multiple Echo skill casts on the team (in her Mono Fusion team, this will typically not be maxed out and be left at 36%, but will go up to the full 60% with Qiuyuan or Lucilla).

And for those who are curious: DMG Taken is the opposite of DMG Reduction observable in Tower of Adversity. They interact with one another directly and are considered the same damage multiplier (they just increment as positive DMG Reduction or Negative DMG Reduction = Vulnerability).

Attacks outside of Demon Hypostasis

Outside of Demon Hypostasis, Galbrena will want to execute a mix of Heavy and Basic Attacks because they replenish her Forte gauge the fastest. As a result, we can exploit the following during her rotations:

  • Intro leads into Basic Attack 2;

  • Heavy Attack 3 can be Dash Cancelled when fired while retaining full damage and Forte generation;

  • Dodge Counter leads into Basic Attack 4 (situational).

Finally, her Ultimate increases the DMG multiplier of all attacks in Demon Hypostasis by 85% which means it is necessary to cast before doing any attacks in Demon Hypostasis, because this buff represents a massive damage boost. However, the 20% DMG Amplify from her Inherent skill should be fully stacked up before using it to maximize damage (simply doing Intro + Basic Attack + Enhanced Skill is sufficient!)

Attacks during Demon Hypostasis

During Demon Hypostasis, Galbrena only has her Basic Attack and Dodge Counter that she should worry about in order to fully expend her Forte gauge. There are 4 different properties to note here:

  • Ultimate leads into Basic Attack 2;

  • Basic Attack 5 leads into Basic Attack 3;

  • Basic Attack 3 can be Dash Cancelled at the end of the animation to save minimal time, Basic Attack 5 can be Dash Cancelled as soon as the enemy is hit by Galbrena’s kick to save a lot of time;

  • Dodge Counter leads into Basic Attack 4.

All of these properties are used in her rotation to skip out on the weak Basic Attack 1 and only focus on the much stronger Basic Attacks 3, 4 and 5 which have much higher damage values than the first two. Additionally, the Dodge Counter is really strong and for all intents and purposes serves as a Basic Attack 3 with higher damage. It can be quite advantageous in the right situations. Starting from max Forte, 2 Dodge Counter combos or 2 full Basic 3,4,5 combos can be executed (alongside a Basic 2 to start with). 

Meta Position & Conclusion

Galbrena is a very simple Basic Attack spam character, whose only real damage ceiling improvements reside in her rotation outside of Demon Hypostasis - where Heavy Attacks do find some use, and her Forte gauge can be generated before Introing into her in certain teams, particularly those involving Lupa to nearly immediately go into Demon Hypostasis after Intro and save time.

Beyond this, she has very little intricacies to her kit and as a result presents herself as a decent Fusion damage dealer with decent teams. But that’s all she is: a decent character all around. Galbrena faces issues in endgame content generally by a lack of damage numbers to keep up with the modern 3.x cast. It’s still quite possible to clear with her, particularly in Quickswap, but generally Galbrena is behind the modern damage dealers and it shows. She was at her prime in version 3.0, when Mornye and Phasic Homogenizer both released to give her a new best team alongside Lupa and a fantastic alternative to her Signature, however since the release of Aemeath right after that, in the Fusion DPS department she was quickly outshined for Lupa teams, or at least Mornye teams since Aemeath’s own best team uses her and Lynae. Additionally, Sigrika came out as a new best user of Qiuyuan. 

While Galbrena is decent in both WhiWa and ToA and can see acceptable results, she generally has all of her best teammates constantly stolen from her by damage dealers with simplt higher baseline numbers, that operate in the same niche that she does. Lucilla is the latest expansion to the Echo Skill damage engine that Galbrena can make use of, but she is no upgrade to Qiuyuan as he gives slightly less specialized buffs than Lucilla, and Galbrena deals 1/3 Heavy Attack damage, which Lucilla does not help with in the slightest.

In conclusion, Galbrena used to be one of the strongest damage dealers when she released, but since then got outshined rather quickly. Landing on the tail end of 2.x damage dealers, the newest generations of damage dealers that came since version 3.1 quickly stole her best teammates to take them to new heights, both in Mono Fusion and in Echo Skill damage, rendering her quite skippable overall for new players, as she remains usable for players who already own her for now.
profile.pros:
• Can play into both the Mono Fusion and Echo Skill DMG archetypes, giving her some decent teammate flexibility;

  • Does not need her Signature weapon at all. Phasic Homogenizer is totally fine as a replacement;

  • Outro being damage-only means she is fully Quickswap-friendly.
profile.cons:
• Her best team is Mono Fusion. Any more modern Fusion DPS than Galbrena can use those characters better than she can, because her raw damage numbers don’t compete;

  • Her other best team is Echo Skill DMG with Qiuyuan/Lucilla. Sigrika is a direct upgrade to Galbrena in all scenarios there, other than Aero RES;

  • TL;DR: Galbrena has no reason to exist on anyone’s account if you don’t already own her and want to find the best fit for your Echo/Fusion Supports.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

The focus of Galbrena’s kit lies on building her 2 Forte resources - Afterflame (in red) and Sinflame (in blue) - to then use them during her Demon Hypostasis state (entered via her Enhanced Skill obtained by fully restoring her Sinflame bar).

To restore Sinflame, the most efficient ways are sometimes Heavy Attacks, but mostly Basic Attacks. Those will also be the core of her damage in Demon Hypostasis. 

To restore Afterflame, it is dependent on Echo skill casts and that is solely provided by casting active Echo skills or having specific teammates like Qiuyuan, Lucilla and Phrolova who have additional attacks that count as Echo skill casts. This means we always want to cast Galbrena’s active Echo Skill before entering Demon Hypostasis to restore Afterflame and expend it during Demon Hypostasis to enhance Galbrena’s damage.

With these factors in mind, below is what her standard rotation may look like:

Standard Rotation

Without featuring any Quickswap, Galbrena can rotate like so:

  • Intro

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Heavy 1

  • Heavy 2

  • Heavy 3 (Cancel animation on shot via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Heavy 1

  • Heavy 2 (Cancel animation as soon as possible via Skill)

  • Skill: Ascent of Malice (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 2

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 3 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 4

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 5 (Cancel animation on kick via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 3 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 4

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 5 (Swap)

  • Outro

Extended Rotation

To extend her rotation by a bit over a second and deal some extra damage, Galbrena can utilize the same exact rotation concept as before but do 1 more Demon Hypostasis attack:

  • Intro

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Heavy 1

  • Heavy 2

  • Heavy 3 (Cancel animation on shot via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Heavy 1

  • Heavy 2 (Cancel animation as soon as possible via Skill)

  • Skill: Ascent of Malice (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 2

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 3 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 4

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 5 (Cancel animation on kick via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 3 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 4

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 5 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash)

  • Dash: Hellstride

  • Basic: Seraphic Execution 3 (Swap)

  • Outro

The main advantage in this rotation is all buffs are retained on the final Basic 5, including Outro buffs that would normally expire on swap, and buffs that apply only to the active character like Qiuyuan’s CRIT DMG & Echo Skill DMG Bonus buffs. Meanwhile, the final Basic 3 gets almost no buffs, as Galbrena executes a Seraphic Execution Basic while Demon Hypostasis has expired. It’s quite weak, but it’s the best you can get while keeping all buffs active on the final Basic 5 that actually deals good damage.

Additional Tips & Tricks

Dodge Counters actually aren’t a big deal for Galbrena to perform, as they are her highest damage multiplier in Demon Hypostasis and act as a significantly enhanced version of her Basic 3. Overall, if needed to execute, while they do extend her rotation time through having to dodge, they aren’t a big deal to perform.

Galbrena’s Ultimate could theoretically be used before her Enhanced Skill, however it deals a high amount of damage and as a result we want to stack up her 20% DMG Amplify effect from her Inherent Passive to optimize damage.

In regard to the above point, while Galbrena’s Basic Attacks before her Enhanced Skill can be performed before her Intro, one Basic Attack always needs to be performed to fully stack up this Inherent Passive effect in time for her Ultimate cast. However, to optimize team rotation time (this is particularly applicable with Lupa on the team since she has many Swap Cancel windows), Galbrena can and should ideally perform a Basic 2,3,4 combo before her Intro at minimum. 

This allows her to cast Basic 2,3 after her Intro and proceed with her rotation as normal, though she can cast these two right before Introing in to get her full buffs and Sinflame charged up before her on-field rotation even begun. Note that Galbrena will always start from her Basic 2 if swapped from any character in combat, whether her Intro is available or not.

skills.name: Slayer's Trigger
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 4 consecutive attacks, dealing Fusion DMG. Basic Attack Stage 1 to 3 DMG are considered as Heavy Attack DMG, and Basic Attack Stage 4 DMG as Echo Skill DMG.

Press Normal Attack right after performing Basic Attack Stage 4 to perform Basic Attack Stage 2.

Heavy Attack - Volley of Death

Consume STA to attack the target and perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Fusion DMG. Stage 3 DMG is considered as Echo Skill DMG.

Press Normal Attack right after performing Heavy Attack - Volley of Death Stage 1 to perform Basic Attack Stage 2. Press Normal Attack right after performing Heavy Attack - Volley of Death Stage 2 or 3 to perform Basic Attack Stage 3.

Mid-air Attack - Ashfall Barrage

While in mid-air, press Normal Attack to consume STA to perform a Plunging Attack, dealing Fusion DMG, considered as Heavy Attack DMG.

While in mid-air, hold Normal Attack to continuously consume STA to launch a barrage of shots at targets below, dealing Fusion DMG, considered as Heavy Attack DMG. If Galbrena does not land when interrupted during the barrage, she cannot immediately cast this skill again. Release Normal Attack during the barrage to cast Plunging Attack.

Press Normal Attack right after casting Plunging Attack to cast Basic Attack Stage 3.

Dodge Counter - Blood for Blood

Press Normal Attack right after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Fusion DMG, considered as Heavy Attack DMG. Press Normal Attack right after casting this skill to cast Basic Attack Stage 4.

skills.name: Beyond Threshold
skills.description:
Threshold State

By default, Galbrena is in Threshold State, and in this state, she accumulates Afterflame and Sinflame.

Demon Hypostasis

While in Demon Hypostasis, Basic Attack, Heavy Attack - Volley of Death, Mid-air Attack - Ashfall Barrage, Dodge Counter - Blood for Blood, and Resonance Skill - Encroach are replaced with Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution, Heavy Attack - Flamewing Verdict, Mid-air Attack - Hellsent Barrage, Dodge Counter - Purgatory Scourge, and Resonance Skill - Ravage, which consume Purging Flame on hit.

While in Demon Hypostasis, every point of Afterflame increases the DMG of Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution, Heavy Attack - Flamewing Verdict, Mid-air Attack - Hellsent Barrage, Resonance Skill - Ravage, and Dodge Counter - Purgatory Scourge by 1.5%, up to 60%, which is removed upon exiting Demon Hypostasis.

When Purging Flame depletes or after staying in Demon Hypostasis for over 50s, Demon Hypostasis ends automatically.

Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution

Perform up to 5 consecutive attacks, dealing Fusion DMG. Consume Purging Flame on hit. Stage 1 to 3 DMG are considered Heavy Attack DMG, and Stage 4 & 5 DMG Echo Skill DMG.

Press Normal Attack after casting Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution Stage 5 to cast Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution Stage 3.

Heavy Attack - Flamewing Verdict

Consume STA to attack the target and perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Fusion DMG. Consume Purging Flame on hit. Stage 3 DMG is considered Echo Skill DMG.

Press Normal Attack after casting Heavy Attack - Flamewing Verdict Stage 1 to cast Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution Stage 2.

Press Normal Attack after casting Heavy Attack - Flamewing Verdict Stage 2 & 3 to cast Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution Stage 3.

Mid-air Attack - Hellsent Barrage

While in mid-air, press Normal Attack to consume STA to perform aerial attacks, dealing Fusion DMG, considered Heavy Attack DMG. Consume Purging Flame on hit.

While in mid-air, hold Normal Attack to continuously consume STA to launch a barrage of shots at targets, dealing Fusion DMG, considered Heavy Attack DMG. Consume Purging Flame on hit. If Galbrena does not land when interrupted during the barrage, she cannot immediately cast this skill again. Release Normal Attack during the barrage to cast Plunging Attack.

Press Normal Attack after the Plunging Attack to cast Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution Stage 3.

Dodge Counter - Purgatory Scourge

Press Normal Attack right after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Fusion DMG, considered Heavy Attack DMG.

Press Normal Attack right after casting this skill to cast Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution Stage 4.

Resonance Skill - Ravage

Dash forward and leap into the air. Flip backward upon hitting the target, dealing Fusion DMG, considered Heavy Attack DMG.

Consume Purging Flame on hit. Resonance Skill - Ravage and Resonance Skill - Encroach share a cooldown.

Hellstride

Press Dodge on the ground while casting Galbrena's own skills to cast Hellstride to deal a fixed amount of Fusion DMG, considered Basic Attack DMG that does not bear any effect from DMG buffs. Hellstride can trigger successful Dodges. Hellstride cannot be cast consecutively.

Casting this skill does not reset the attack cycles within a short period of time.

Burning Drive

Casting Intro Skill, Hellstride, Normal Attack - Seraphic Execution Basic Attack Stage 4, Resonance Skill - Encroach, Resonance Skill - Ascent of Malice, and Resonance Skill - Ravage increases Galbrena's resistance to interruptions and ATK by 20% for 4s.

Afterflame

Galbrena can hold up to 40 points of Afterflame.

While in Threshold State, Galbrena recovers 8 points of Afterflame when Resonators in the nearby team cast Echo Skill. Echoes with the same name can only trigger this effect once. This effect resets when Galbrena exits Demon Hypostasis.

All Afterflame is removed upon exiting Demon Hypostasis.

Sinflame

Galbrena can hold up to 100 points of Sinflame.

While in Threshold State, hitting an enemy with Basic Attack, Heavy Attack - Volley of Death, Mid-air Attack - Ashfall Barrage, Resonance Skill - Encroach, and Intro Skill - Hellflare Overload recovers Sinflame.

skills.description:
1 stack of Fated End is inflicted on the target when the following skills hit: Intro Skill, Basic Attack, Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution, Dodge Counter, Heavy Attack - Volley of Death, Heavy Attack - Flamewing Verdict, Mid-air Attack, Hellstride, Resonance Skill - Encroach, Resonance Skill - Ascent of Malice, Resonance Skill - Ravage and Resonance Liberation, up to 4 stacks.

weapons.Comment: Galbrena's Signature Weapon has great base stats and a passive focusing around giving Damage Amplify to Heavy Attacks and Echo Skills in tandem with one another. When both effects are stacked, it even gives a small DEF Ignore boost to further increase this weapon's potential. Overall this is her best choice easily.

An amazing generalist permanently available pistol that can universally improve the wearer's ATK, DMG Bonus and CRIT DMG. Can get close to a lot of character signatures and is overall a must-have for most accounts.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Galbrena who does not benefit from this weapon's Tune Break and Basic DMG-focused effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Galbrena, who does not benefit from this weapon's Skill DMG-increasing effects.

The standard banner 5-star is a great choice for Galbrena, having a fully utilized passive in Mono Fusion teams to buff the next incoming character's damage (Lupa for example), while still being generally useful via its high Base ATK, CRIT Rate and Energy Regen stats in any team. This makes it not face significant drop-offs compared to her Signature weapon, which isn't necessary to clear endgame contents thanks to Static Mist, provided Galbrena has good teammates to back her up.
Simple stat-stick for Galbrena, who does not benefit from this weapon's Aero Erosion-focused effects.

This Battle Pass exclusive provides a good CRIT Rate stat as well as a ramp-up ATK and Heavy ATK DMG increase when dealing Basic or Heavy Attack DMG, all fantastic stats for Galbrena. However, it isn't as strong as any 5-star choice due to its lower Base ATK than the choices above.

Overall a great 4-star choice for Galbrena who needs a slight amount of Energy. This weapon's passive increases ATK and restores flat Energy when casting Skill, which makes it a solid choice for her as it makes her not require any Energy Regen substats, although it's not comparable to any 5-star.

The best no-gacha option, this craftable 4-star provides extra ATK over time assuming you don't get hit. This weapon will perform worse than calculated if Galbrena gets hit by enemies often, however it should still outclass any other option than the ones listed above.

synergies.Comment: Galbrena's best Echo Damage buffers that provide multiple Echo Skill casts to fill up her Afterflame gauge, and amplify her Echo DMG via their Outros and other passives/weapon effects. Qiuyuan overall wins out by a slight margin as he sports buffs that apply more to Galbrena's 1/3 Heavy 2/3 Echo DMG split, whereas Lucilla really hones in on Echo DMG.

These 3 are the Mono Fusion team members for Galbrena, an archetype enabled by Lupa's insane buffs catered towards Fusion characters, particularly if the team is only comprised of them. Brant and Mortefi are great Outro buffers for Galbrena since they have 20% Fusion and 38 Heavy DMG Amplification respectively. Brant has higher personal damage which makes him perform at higher investments, but Mortefi is a totally fine alternative, and can even be considered for F2P Galbrena teams. Mono Fusion enabled by Lupa is one of Galbrena's best teams, particularly in Whimpering Wastes, and is definitely worth trying out!

Not Galbrena's best teammate choices, but in Galbrena teams Phrolova and Iuno respectively provide 25 and 50% Heavy DMG Amplification on their Outros, and they both deal very high personal damage. Phrolova is stronger than Iuno in the personal damage department and has an extra Echo Skill cast for Galbrena's Afterflame, so she tends to outclass Iuno for these reasons; however Iuno has a really easy rotation and extra healing if it is preferred. Rebecca is also a generalist Heavy DMG buffer with minimal upsides beyond that, but all of them can be worth considering if the above options are missing.

These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Galbrena and Lupa because she enables Galbrena to work in a Hypercarry team while still sporting Lupa's full Mono Fusion buffs which makes her the best choice if that's available. Otherwise, Shorekeeper is amazing thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.
